lines.text: Meet ChargeOne. It plans any electric car road trip in India: chargers that drivers report working, food while you charge, and a hotel for the night.
On your first visit, ChargeOne shows exactly where its data comes from. Real chargers from open map data, and live status from drivers who are standing at the charger.
Every charger is on one map, from every company. Green means a driver charged there recently, amber means it's busy, and red means a problem was reported.
Need a fast charger? One tap shows only DC fast chargers. You can also filter by connector, twenty-four seven, or operator.
Food and hotels are built in. Orange pins are places to eat, purple pins are hotels, and hotels with a charger on site get a teal ring.
Tap any charger to see when it last worked, at what speed, and what drivers reported this week.
While your car charges, see what's nearby to eat, with walking time, pure veg badges, opening hours, and one-tap directions.
Switch to stays for hotels within three kilometres. Hotels with a charger on site come first, and Check prices opens that exact hotel on Booking dot com.
Every hotel and restaurant has its own page too, with the chargers within walking distance and their live status.
Sign in with Google in one tap.
Drivers at the charger report how it went. Reports are location checked, so they come from people who are really there.
And the charger's status updates for every driver.
Now let's plan a real road trip: Bengaluru to Kochi, about five hundred kilometres.
Pick your car. ChargeOne knows the real-world range of popular Indian electric cars.
On the free plan, multi-day trips are locked, and the app shows you exactly which plan unlocks them.
The free plan covers trips up to one hundred kilometres. For this trip, ChargeOne shows precisely what each plan gives you.

Plus is one hundred and forty-nine rupees a month. Thirty long trips a month at any distance, backup chargers, multi-day plans with hotels, an alert in the app if a charger on your route breaks, and saved trips that open with no signal.
Pay yearly and save forty-four percent.
Or take Trip Pass, forty-nine rupees once, for a single road trip: ten long trips within seven days. It includes backups and multi-day plans, but not alerts or saved trips.
Everything is compared side by side, so there are no surprises. Payment runs on Razorpay with UPI or cards, and you can cancel any time.
Let's choose Plus. This demo uses test mode. The live app pays through Razorpay.
Multi-day trips are now unlocked. Drive up to six hours a day, and ChargeOne finds where to spend the night.
Done. A two-day trip with one charging stop and one overnight stay. Arrival battery, charging time and cost, all worked out.
Because this is Plus, alerts are on. If a stop on your route is reported broken while the trip is open, you'll see it here with a one-tap re-plan.
Here's the route on the map. Numbered pins are charging stops, N one is the overnight stop, and purple pins are hotels.
When a stop has a backup charger nearby, it's listed too, in case the first one is busy or down.
And here's food near the charging stop, a short walk from the charger.
Night one. Arrive, plug in, and you're at a hundred percent by morning. Hotels with a charger on site are listed first.
Get directions, call the hotel, read reviews, or check prices, in one tap.
Day two starts with a full battery, and each day gets its own Google Maps navigation.
Staying at your destination? Here are hotels near Kochi with charging on site or a short walk away.
Plus members can save the trip on their phone, so it opens even where there's no signal.
ChargeOne also has a page for every city and every charger, built to be found on Google.
Your account shows your plan, the trips you have left, and everything it includes. Cancel, or delete your data, any time.
And there's dark mode for night drives.
ChargeOne. Chargers, food and hotels for your whole road trip, in one app. Start free, and upgrade only when you drive out of town.
